title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a framework to coordinate the development and deployment of AI‑driven physical systems, ensuring safety, interoperability, and compliance with national standards. It creates a regulatory body tasked with overseeing compliance, risk assessment, and data transparency for AI technologies integrated into physical infrastructure.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The bill seeks to update the Federal Election Campaign Act so that political ads must clearly disclose if any AI-generated images or videos were used. This requirement aims to increase transparency and hold campaigns accountable for the content they present to voters.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of AI-generated content that could mislead voters. It establishes guidelines and enforcement mechanisms to detect and counter deceptive AI practices that might influence electoral outcomes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes rules for tracking and regulating AI systems that can change and enhance themselves without human intervention. It requires developers to report changes, set safety safeguards, and create oversight mechanisms to ensure these systems remain aligned with public interests and do not pose uncontrolled risks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes temporarily stopping the building and operation of new AI data centers until clear rules on energy use, emissions, and security are in place. It aims to make sure the growth of AI infrastructure does not outpace environmental protection or regulatory standards.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is proposed legislation designed to prevent the deployment of autonomous AI systems that could act unpredictably or harmfully. It would establish strict safety testing, oversight, and liability standards for AI developers and operators to ensure responsible use.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board tasked with investigating and analyzing incidents where artificial intelligence intersects with cybersecurity threats. It aims to enhance transparency, coordinate response efforts, and develop guidelines to improve national resilience against AI-driven cyber attacks.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The “Make AI Work for Americans Act” proposes to guide the development and deployment of artificial intelligence so it benefits the public, emphasizing transparency, safety, and equitable access. It seeks to encourage innovation while protecting citizens’ rights, privacy, and jobs through oversight and regulation.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act mandates the creation of comprehensive reports on artificial intelligence capabilities and deployments within the country, aiming to assess both technological progress and societal impact. It requires regular disclosure to government bodies and may include guidelines for transparency, accountability, and regulatory oversight.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 bars artificial‑intelligence systems from diagnosing or treating patients without direct oversight by a licensed medical professional. It establishes legal standards and penalties to keep medical decision‑making in the hands of human doctors.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The bill would create a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the President’s Executive Office, aimed at monitoring and addressing risks from AI and other emerging technologies. It also includes additional, unspecified provisions for related purposes.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to establish clear guidelines and standards for AI research to ensure that AI systems are trustworthy, safe, and reliable. It sets requirements for rigorous testing, transparency, and accountability so that AI developers and users can evaluate and deploy AI technologies responsibly.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to protect AI systems from cyber threats. The act outlines plans to develop guidelines, standards, and coordination mechanisms to reduce AI-related security risks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to create clear rules for identifying and reducing the risks of AI systems. It aims to improve safety and accountability by requiring companies to assess AI risks, disclose how models work, and follow oversight procedures.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to review and shape the nation's AI strategy. The committee will examine AI’s benefits, risks, and regulatory needs, and recommend actions to lawmakers.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 would create rules for assessing the safety and potential harm of AI systems. It is expected to require companies to evaluate AI risks, report findings, and follow guidelines to protect public welfare.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed European Union law that aims to set clear rules for how artificial intelligence can be developed, deployed, and used. It focuses on making AI safer and more transparent by requiring companies to assess risks, provide explanations for decisions, and protect users’ privacy and fundamental rights.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies. It requires companies to assess and report the energy consumption, carbon emissions, and resource use of AI systems, and imposes penalties for non‑compliance.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed artificial‑intelligence education into primary and secondary school curricula, ensuring that students acquire the skills to understand, use, and critically evaluate AI tools. It also aims to give teachers professional development and resources so they can effectively integrate AI concepts into their lesson plans, building a generation of AI‑literary, ethically aware learners.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a federal law designed to ensure AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and reliable before they reach the public. It establishes standards and oversight mechanisms for AI research and development, requiring rigorous testing, transparency, and accountability from developers and companies.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. It also includes additional measures to support broader national cybersecurity efforts.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that requires schools to build AI education into their curricula to help students understand how AI works and how to use it responsibly. It also calls for training teachers, developing resources, and ensuring schools are ready to safely integrate AI technology into learning.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to regulate how artificial‑intelligence systems are used in processing Veterans Affairs claims. It seeks to make those systems transparent, fair, and subject to oversight so that veterans receive accurate and unbiased decisions.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: This act requires the Veterans Affairs department to disclose how AI is used and keep the public informed about its performance. It also likely sets rules for testing, reporting, and protecting veterans’ data when AI is applied.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is a law that seeks to boost the public’s knowledge and understanding of artificial intelligence. It proposes creating outreach programs, educational resources, and national campaigns so people can learn about AI’s benefits, risks, and responsible use.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate has adopted a resolution that emphasizes protecting religious freedom and the integrity of authoritative texts in the context of AI. It also calls for greater transparency in artificial intelligence systems to ensure they respect these principles.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act aims to safeguard consumers by requiring clear labeling and disclosure for AI-generated content, ensuring they can identify when they are interacting with or viewing AI‑produced material. It also establishes penalties for deceptive AI practices and provides a framework for consumer complaints and enforcement.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are employed to acquire, analyze, query, or disseminate information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. This report aims to provide oversight and transparency about AI’s role in foreign intelligence activities.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to improve AI literacy and skillsets among students and workers so they can thrive in an AI-driven economy. It proposes funding for curriculum development, teacher training, and workforce programs to close the current skills gap.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that would encourage the development and use of open‑source AI software, making it easier for companies, universities, and the public to share AI tools and data. It aims to create a framework for collaboration, transparency, and competition while protecting intellectual property and ensuring that AI technologies remain accessible and beneficial to society.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to curb artificial intelligence firms from inflating service costs and manipulating wages through algorithmic pricing. It sets rules and penalties to promote fair competition, protect consumers, and uphold transparent labor practices.
